messages:
Maya R: Quick sync — I want to propose a change to how we store routing identifiers in console telemetry. Current problem: route_id is numeric, but we now need stable logical ids that survive renames/aliasing. Thinking route_logical_id (text) + deterministic alias mapping.

Jon P: Sounds reasonable. What's the migration plan? major downtime? :eyes:

Maya R: No downtime target. Plan: add new column, start dual-write at ingest for N days, populate via backfill query, then flip reads to prefer route_logical_id. Fallback to route_id when missing.

Sasha L: Dual-write + read adapter is safer. Need a compatibility layer in the console API so dashboards don't break during the window.

Arjun K: Agree. Also watch index sizes — route_logical_id is text so we should hash-prefix it for partitioning. Propose creating a computed column route_logical_hash bigint for sharding.

Maya R: Good call. Draft SQL for the add + index: ```sql
ALTER TABLE console_events
  ADD COLUMN route_logical_id text,
  ADD COLUMN route_logical_hash bigint;

UPDATE console_events
  SET route_logical_id = COALESCE(route_alias, route_id::text)
  WHERE route_logical_id IS NULL;

UPDATE console_events
  SET route_logical_hash = ('x' || substr(md5(route_logical_id),1,16))::bit(64)::bigint
  WHERE route_logical_hash IS NULL;

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ON console_events (route_logical_hash);
```

Jon P: Nice. Two nits: 1) CONCURRENTLY will still escalate locks for very large tables depending on DB. We should test on a shadow table. 2) Backfill should be batched to avoid replication lag.

Sasha L: For the read adapter: implement route_resolution middleware in console-api that does: prefer route_logical_id, if null call a lightweight resolver service that maps old route_id -> logical id. That lets us cutover on a per-client basis.

Arjun K: Monitoring/telemetry: add a metric route_migration_read_preference with counts for {legacy,logical,resolved} so we can see if lookup failures spike. Also add a dashboard tile showing per-tenant percent of rows with route_logical_id populated.

Maya R: Will add those to the plan. Rollout steps I'm thinking: 1) schema add columns (no index), 2) enable dual-write in ingest pipeline behind feature flag, 3) start background backfill (batched), 4) create index CONCURRENTLY when backfill at 95% for active tenants, 5) enable read adapter to prefer logical id for internal console routes, 6) remove legacy code after 30d.

Jon P: What about queries that GROUP BY route_id in analytics jobs? Those need mapping to route_logical_id too or temporary alias views. Could break long-running jobs.

Sasha L: Suggest creating a materialized view analytics.events_by_route_logical that rewrites GROUP BYs and keeps incremental refresh. Jobs can switch to new view. Also mark all long-running ETL owners in a migration announcement.

Maya R: I'll draft the announcement and migration playbook. Also adding rollback: disable dual-write and revert read adapter to old behavior, keep columns for audit.

DevEx Bot: migration-checklist created: https://internal.redwood/migrations/1749004321. Steps + runbook linked. :white_check_mark:

Arjun K: One more: ACLs and RBAC — some older dashboards reference numeric ids in saved queries. We'll need UI migration helpers to rebind saved queries to logical ids or surface a migration warning in Dashboard settings.

Maya R: Good catch. I'll loop in product for saved-query migration UX. If no objections, I'll kick off a small shadow backfill tomorrow and post the results. :shipit:

Jon P: 👍 Do it. Keep me posted on the backfill perf numbers and index growth.

Sasha L: I'll prep the read adapter PR and the dashboard metric tile.

Maya R: Thanks all — posting the detailed playbook in #eng-platform once the shadow run completes.
